title.zh: 卷一百三十三 列傳第八十三: 李晟
title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第八十三: 李晟 Volume 133 Biographies 83: Li Cheng

sentences.zh: 徐浩徐浩，字季海，越州人。

translations.literal: Xu Hao, styled Jihai, was a native of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao, whose courtesy name was Jihai, came from Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 父嶠，官至洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jiao reached the office of Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu Jiao had served as prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 浩少舉明經，工草隸，以文學為張說所器重，調授魯山主簿。

translations.literal: In his youth Hao passed the Mingjing examination, excelled in cursive and clerical script, and for his literary talent was highly regarded by Zhang Yue; he was appointed registrar of Lushan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Xu Hao passed the Classics examination and was skilled in cursive and clerical calligraphy. Zhang Yue valued his literary gifts and had him appointed registrar of Lushan.

sentences.zh: 說薦為麗正殿校理，三遷右拾遺，仍為校理。

translations.literal: Yue recommended him as collator of the Lizheng Hall, and after three promotions he became Right Reminder, while still serving as collator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue recommended him as a collator in the Hall for the Rectification of Literature. After three promotions he became Right Reminder, yet continued to serve as collator.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度使張守珪奏在幕府，改監察御史。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Youzhou, Zhang Shougui, memorialized that he serve on his staff, and he was changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Youzhou, had him serve on his staff, after which he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，授京兆司錄，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he was appointed recorder of the capital district, then left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, and when it ended he was made recorder of the capital district. He later resigned to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 數年，調授河南司錄，歷河陽令，以善政稱。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred and appointed recorder of Henan, served as magistrate of Heyang, and was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was transferred to recorder of Henan and then served as magistrate of Heyang, where his good administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 拜太子司議郎，遷金部員外郎，歷憲部郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed adviser to the heir apparent, promoted to vice director of the Department of Revenue, and served as director in the Department of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed adviser to the crown prince, then promoted to vice director in the Department of Revenue and later served as a director in the Department of Justice.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，出為襄陽太守、本郡防禦使，賜以金紫之服。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, he went out as prefect of Xiangyang and defense commissioner of that commandery, and was granted gold-and-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, he was sent out as prefect of Xiangyang and defense commissioner of the commandery, and was granted the gold-and-purple insignia of high rank.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，召拜中書舍人，時天下事殷，詔令多出于浩。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, Hao was summoned and appointed drafting secretary; affairs under heaven were pressing, and many edicts issued from Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong came to the throne, Xu Hao was summoned and made drafting secretary. With the empire in crisis, many of the court's edicts came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 浩屬詞贍給，又工楷隸，肅宗悅其能，加兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Hao's compositions were rich and fluent, and he was also skilled in regular and clerical script; Suzong delighted in his ability and additionally made him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hao wrote with abundant fluency and was also accomplished in regular and clerical calligraphy. Emperor Suzong admired his talents and additionally appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 玄宗傳位誥冊，皆浩為之，參兩宮文翰，寵遇罕與為比。

translations.literal: The abdication proclamations of Emperor Xuanzong were all composed by Hao; he took part in the literary affairs of both palaces, and favor shown him was rarely matched.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted all the abdication documents when Emperor Xuanzong transferred the throne, handled literary affairs for both the retired and reigning sovereigns, and enjoyed favor seldom equaled at court.

sentences.zh: 除國子祭酒，坐事貶廬州長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the Directorate of Education, then for an offense was demoted to chief administrator of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Directorate of Education, but after an offense was demoted to chief administrator of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗征拜中書舍人、集賢殿學士，尋遷工部侍郎、嶺南節度觀察使、兼御史大夫，又為吏部侍郎、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong summoned and appointed him drafting secretary and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; soon he was promoted to vice minister of works, military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan, and concurrently censor-in-chief, then served again as vice minister of personnel and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong summoned him back as drafting secretary and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. He was soon promoted to vice minister of works, then made military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan with the concurrent title of censor-in-chief, and later served again as vice minister of personnel and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 坐以妾弟冒選，托侍郎薛邕註授京尉，為御史大夫李棲筠所彈，坐貶明州別駕。

translations.literal: For having his younger brother by a concubine fraudulently entered in selection and entrusting Vice Minister Xue Yong to register him for a capital district post, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Qiyun and demoted to assistant prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Qiyun after arranging, through Vice Minister Xue Yong, a fraudulent appointment for his younger half-brother as a capital district officer, and was demoted to assistant prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，征拜彭王傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Hao was summoned and appointed tutor to the Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong came to the throne, Xu Hao was summoned and appointed tutor to the Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 建中三年，以疾卒，年八十，贈太子少師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died of illness at age eighty, and was posthumously made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianzhong era he died of illness at the age of eighty and was posthumously honored as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，浩以文雅稱；

translations.literal: At first Hao was known for refined literary talent;
translations.idiomatic: At first Xu Hao was known for his refined literary gifts;

sentences.zh: 及授廣州，典選部，多積貨財，又嬖其妾侯莫陳氏，頗幹政事，為時論所貶。

translations.literal: but once appointed to Guangzhou and put in charge of the selection bureau, he amassed much wealth, favored his concubine of the Houmo Chen clan, and meddled considerably in government affairs, and was disparaged in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: but after he was sent to Guangzhou and placed in charge of the selection bureau, he amassed great wealth, favored his concubine of the Houmo Chen clan, and meddled heavily in affairs of state, drawing widespread criticism.

sentences.zh: 趙涓趙涓，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Juan was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼有文學。

translations.literal: From youth he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，舉進士，補郾城尉，累授監察御史、右司員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Yancheng, and successively received appointment as investigating censor and vice director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Yancheng, then rose to investigating censor and vice director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 河南副元帥王縉奏充判官，授檢校兵部郎中、兼侍御史，遷給事中、太常少卿，出為衢州刺史。

translations.literal: The deputy commander-in-chief of Henan, Wang Jin, memorialized him as staff judge; he was appointed acting director in the Ministry of War and concurrently attendant censor, promoted to supervising secretary and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and went out as prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, deputy commander-in-chief of Henan, had him serve as staff judge. He was appointed acting director in the Ministry of War with the concurrent post of attendant censor, then promoted to supervising secretary and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices before being sent out as prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，涓為監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongtai era Juan was an investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongtai era Zhao Juan served as an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時禁中失火，燒屋室數十間，火發處與東宮稍近，代宗深疑之，涓為巡使，俾令即訊。

translations.literal: At that time a fire broke out in the inner palace and burned several dozen rooms; the place where the fire started was rather near the Eastern Palace, and Emperor Daizong was deeply suspicious; Juan was made touring commissioner and ordered to investigate at once.
translations.idiomatic: When a fire broke out in the inner palace and burned several dozen rooms, the blaze began uncomfortably close to the Eastern Palace. Emperor Daizong was deeply suspicious and appointed Zhao Juan touring commissioner with orders to investigate immediately.

sentences.zh: 涓周歷需囿，按據跡狀，乃上直中官遺火所致也，推鞫明審，頗盡事情。

translations.literal: Juan went all through the palace grounds, followed the traces, and found that it had been caused by a eunuch on palace duty who had left a fire; his examination was clear and thorough, and largely brought out the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan searched the palace grounds, followed the evidence, and determined that a eunuch on palace duty had left a fire unattended. His inquiry was thorough and clear, and largely brought the matter to light.

sentences.zh: 既奏，代宗稱賞焉。

translations.literal: After he reported, Daizong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported his findings, Emperor Daizong praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 德宗時在東宮，常感涓之究理詳細，及刺衢州，年考既深，又與觀察使韓滉不相得，滉奏免涓官，德宗見其名，謂宰臣曰：「豈非永泰初御史趙涓乎？

translations.literal: Dezong was then in the Eastern Palace and had often been impressed by Juan's detailed investigation; when Juan was prefect of Quzhou his years of service were already long, and he also did not get along with the observation commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized to remove Juan from office; Dezong saw his name and said to the chief ministers, "Is this not the censor Zhao Juan of early Yongtai?"
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, then crown prince, had long admired Zhao Juan's meticulous investigation. Later, as prefect of Quzhou, Juan had deep seniority but clashed with observation commissioner Han Huang, who memorialized for his removal. When Dezong saw the name on the memorial, he asked his chief ministers, "Is this not Zhao Juan, the censor from early Yongtai?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「然。

translations.literal: They replied, "It is."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 」即拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Juan was immediately appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 無何，知吏部選，扈從梁州。

translations.literal: Before long he was put in charge of personnel selection and accompanied the court to Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was placed in charge of personnel selection and accompanied the court to Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan he died and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Xingyuan era and was posthumously honored as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子 博宣子博宣，登進士第，文章俊拔，性率多酒。

translations.literal: His son Bozhuan passed the jinshi examination; his writing was outstanding, and by nature he was frank and fond of wine.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao Bozhuan passed the jinshi examination. His writing was outstanding, and by nature he was forthright and fond of drink.

sentences.zh: 陳許節度使曲環辟為從事，賓筵之間多所忽略，環不能容。

translations.literal: The military commissioner of Chenxu, Qu Huan, recruited him as staff officer; at banquets he often showed neglect, and Huan could not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Huan, military commissioner of Chenxu, recruited him as a staff officer, but Bozhuan often showed disrespect at banquets, which Qu Huan could not abide.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方討淮、蔡，環誣奏博宣受吳少誠賂為反間，又妄說國家休咎，扇惑軍情。

translations.literal: The court was then campaigning against Huai and Cai; Huan falsely memorialized that Bozhuan had taken bribes from Wu Shaocheng to act as a spy, and also spoke recklessly of the state's fortunes and misfortunes, stirring up the army's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was campaigning against Huai and Cai, Qu Huan falsely accused Bozhuan of taking bribes from Wu Shaocheng to serve as a spy, and of recklessly prophesying the state's fortunes and stirring up the troops.

sentences.zh: 時博宣權知舞陽縣事，詔令環決杖四十，流於康州，人皆以為枉。

translations.literal: At the time Bozhuan was acting magistrate of Wuyang; an edict ordered Huan to have him beaten forty strokes and exiled to Kangzhou, and people all regarded it as unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhuan was then acting magistrate of Wuyang. An edict authorized Qu Huan to have him beaten forty strokes and exiled to Kangzhou, and most considered the punishment unjust.

sentences.zh: 先是，侍御史盧南史坐事貶信州員外司馬，至郡，準例得廳吏一人，每月請紙筆錢，前後五年，計錢一千貫。

translations.literal: Earlier, attendant censor Lu Nanshi, punished for an offense, was demoted to supernumerary militia commander of Xinzhou; on reaching the prefecture, by regulation he was entitled to one office clerk, who each month requested paper-and-brush money; over five years this totaled one thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, attendant censor Lu Nanshi had been demoted for an offense to supernumerary militia commander of Xinzhou. On reaching his post he was entitled by regulation to one office clerk, who for five years had collected paper-and-brush allowances totaling one thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 南史以官閑冗，放吏歸，納其紙筆錢六十余千。

translations.literal: Nanshi, finding his post idle and superfluous, released the clerk and turned in more than sixty thousand of the paper-and-brush money.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his post largely idle, Lu Nanshi released the clerk and turned in more than sixty thousand cash of the collected allowances.

sentences.zh: 刺史姚驥劾奏南史，以為贓，又劾南史買鉛燒黃丹。

translations.literal: Prefect Yao Ji impeached Nanshi for corruption, and also impeached him for buying lead and smelting yellow cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yao Ji impeached Lu Nanshi for corruption and also accused him of buying lead to smelt yellow cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣監察御史鄭楚相、刑部員外郎裴澥、大理評事陳正儀充三司使，同往按鞫。

translations.literal: Dezong sent investigating censor Zheng Chuxiang, vice director of the Ministry of Justice Pei Xie, and reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review Chen Zhengyi as the three-commissioner envoys to investigate together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong dispatched investigating censor Zheng Chuxiang, vice director of the Ministry of Justice Pei Xie, and Court of Judicial Review reviewer Chen Zhengyi as a three-commissioner team to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 將行，並召於延英，謂之曰：「卿等必須詳審，無令漏罪銜冤。

translations.literal: Before they set out, all were summoned to Yanying and told, "You must examine carefully and not let crimes escape or injustice remain."
translations.idiomatic: Before they departed, all three were summoned to the Yanying Hall and told, "You must investigate carefully and see that no crime goes unpunished and no innocent man bears blame."

sentences.zh: 」三人將退，裴澥獨留，奏曰：「臣按姚驥奏狀，稱南史取廳吏紙筆錢計贓六十余貫，雖於公法有違，量事且非巨蠹。

translations.literal: As the three were about to withdraw, Pei Xie alone remained and memorialized, "According to Prefect Yao Ji's report, Nanshi is charged with taking the clerk's paper-and-brush money, totaling more than sixty strings as corruption; though this violates public law, measured by the matter it is not a great evil."
translations.idiomatic: As the three were about to withdraw, Pei Xie alone remained and said, "According to Prefect Yao Ji's report, Lu Nanshi is accused of taking the clerk's paper-and-brush money—more than sixty strings—as graft. Though this violates the law, the offense is hardly a major corruption case."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此事亦未為甚，未知燒鉛何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This matter too is not very serious; I do not know how the smelting of lead stands?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That matter is not very serious either. What about the charge of smelting lead?"

sentences.zh: 」澥曰：「燒鉛為丹，格令不禁。

translations.literal: Xie said, "Smelting lead into cinnabar is not forbidden by statute."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xie said, "Smelting lead into cinnabar is not forbidden by statute."

sentences.zh: 準天寶十三載敕，鉛、銅、錫不許私家買賣貨易，蓋防私鑄錢，本亦不言燒鉛為丹。

translations.literal: According to the edict of the thirteenth year of Tianbao, lead, copper, and tin may not be bought or sold privately, to guard against illicit coining; it does not in itself speak of smelting lead into cinnabar.
translations.idiomatic: The edict of the thirteenth year of Tianbao forbids private trade in lead, copper, and tin to prevent illicit coining; it says nothing about smelting lead into cinnabar.

sentences.zh: 南史違敕買鉛，不得無罪。

translations.literal: Nanshi violated the edict in buying lead and cannot be without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Nanshi did violate the edict by buying lead and cannot be held entirely blameless.

sentences.zh: 伏以陛下自登寶位，及天寶、大歷以來，未曾降三司使至江南；

translations.literal: I submit that since Your Majesty ascended the throne, and since Tianbao and Dali, a three-commissioner envoy has never been sent to the south of the Yangtze;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that since Your Majesty took the throne—and indeed since the Tianbao and Dali eras—a three-commissioner envoy has never been sent to the Jiangnan region;

sentences.zh: 今忽錄此小事，令三司使往，非唯損耗州縣，亦恐遠處聞之，各懷憂懼。

translations.literal: now suddenly to take up this small matter and send a three-commissioner envoy will not only drain the prefectures and districts, but also, I fear, when distant places hear of it, each will harbor anxiety and fear.
translations.idiomatic: to dispatch a three-commissioner team for so minor a matter will not only burden the local administrations but may alarm distant regions when they hear of it.

sentences.zh: 臣聞開元中張九齡為五嶺按察使，有錄事參軍告齡非法，朝廷止令大理評事往按。

translations.literal: I have heard that in the Kaiyuan era Zhang Jiuling was inspection commissioner of the Five Ridges; when a registrar reported Jiuling's illegal acts, the court only sent a reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era, when a registrar accused Zhang Jiuling, then inspection commissioner of the Five Ridges, of illegal conduct, the court sent only a Court of Judicial Review reviewer to investigate.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，鄂嶽觀察使吳仲孺與轉運使判官劉長卿紛競，仲孺奏長卿犯贓二十萬貫，時止差監察御史苗伾就推。

translations.literal: In the Dali era the observation commissioner of E-Yue, Wu Zhongru, quarreled with the transport commissioner staff judge Liu Changqing; Zhongru memorialized that Changqing had committed corruption of two hundred thousand strings, and at the time only investigating censor Miao Pi was sent to examine.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, when observation commissioner Wu Zhongru of E-Yue quarreled with transport commissioner staff judge Liu Changqing and accused him of two hundred thousand strings in graft, the court sent only investigating censor Miao Pi to examine the case.

sentences.zh: 今姚驥所奏事狀無多，臣堪任此行，即請獨往，恐不須三司並行為使。

translations.literal: The matters reported by Yao Ji are not many; I am fit for this mission and ask to go alone—I fear there is no need for all three commissioners to go together.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Yao Ji's charges are slight, and I am fit for this mission. I ask to go alone; there is no need for all three commissioners to travel together.

sentences.zh: 」德宗忻然曰：「卿言是矣。

translations.literal: Dezong said with pleasure, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong said with pleasure, "You are quite right."

sentences.zh: 」乃復召楚相、正儀與澥俱坐，謂之曰：「朕懵於理道，處事未精，適見裴澥所奏，深協事宜，亦不用三人總去，但行首一人行可也，卿等使宣付宰臣改敕。

translations.literal: He then summoned Chuxiang, Zhengyi, and Xie to sit together and said, "I am dull in the Way of governance and not yet skilled in handling affairs; what I have just heard from Pei Xie's memorial deeply fits the situation. There is no need for all three to go—only the chief commissioner need go. You shall announce this and have the chief ministers revise the edict."
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Zheng Chuxiang, Chen Zhengyi, and Pei Xie and said, "I am still unskilled in governance. Pei Xie's memorial fits the situation well. All three of you need not go—only the lead commissioner will suffice. Announce this and have the chief ministers revise the edict."

sentences.zh: 」德宗不務大體，以察為明，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Dezong did not attend to the larger pattern and took minute scrutiny for wisdom—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong neglected the larger pattern of governance and mistook minute scrutiny for wisdom; this was typical of his rule.

sentences.zh: 而博宣、南史坐誣枉擯逐，賴裴澥悟主，南史不至深罪，後得召還。

translations.literal: Bozhuan and Nanshi suffered false charges and wrongful removal; thanks to Pei Xie's enlightening the sovereign, Nanshi did not receive deep punishment and was later summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhuan and Nanshi were wrongly driven out on false charges. Thanks to Pei Xie's persuasion of the emperor, Nanshi escaped severe punishment and was later recalled.

sentences.zh: 劉太真劉太真，宣州人。

translations.literal: Liu Taizhen was a native of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taizhen came from Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 涉學，善屬文，少師事詞人蕭穎士。

translations.literal: He studied broadly, was skilled in composition, and in youth took the poet Xiao Yingshi as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned and skilled at composition; in his youth he studied under the poet Xiao Yingshi.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，為淮南節度使陳少遊掌書記，征拜起居郎。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he served as secretary to the military commissioner of Huainan, Chen Shaoyou, and was summoned as attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era he served as secretary to Chen Shaoyou, military commissioner of Huainan, and was summoned to the post of attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 累歷臺閣，自中書舍人轉工部、刑部二侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served in the central offices, moving from drafting secretary to vice ministers of works and of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the central offices, moving from drafting secretary to vice minister of works and then vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 性怯懦詭隨。

translations.literal: By nature he was timid, cowardly, and evasive.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was timid, evasive, and given to shifting with circumstances.

sentences.zh: 及轉禮部侍郎，掌貢舉，宰執姻族，方鎮子弟，先收擢之。

translations.literal: When he became vice minister of rites and took charge of the examinations, he first selected and promoted the kin of chief ministers and the sons of regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When he became vice minister of rites and took charge of the civil service examinations, he gave priority to the kin of chief ministers and the sons of regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 又常敘少遊勛績，擬之桓、文，大招物論。

translations.literal: He also often recounted Shaoyou's achievements and compared him to Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi, greatly provoking public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: He also often praised Chen Shaoyou's achievements and compared him to Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi, drawing widespread criticism.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，貶信州刺史，到州尋卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou and died soon after reaching the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan he was demoted to prefect of Xinzhou and died soon after arriving.

sentences.zh: 太真尤長於詩句，每出一篇，人皆諷誦。

translations.literal: Taizhen was especially skilled in verse; whenever he produced a piece, people all recited it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Taizhen was especially gifted in verse; whenever he published a new poem, people recited it throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 德宗文思俊拔，每有禦制，即命朝臣畢和。

translations.literal: Dezong's literary thought was outstanding; whenever he had an imperial composition, he ordered all the court officials to compose matching pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong wrote with outstanding literary talent; whenever he composed an imperial poem, he ordered the entire court to write matching verses.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年九月，賜宴曲江亭，帝為詩，序曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan he granted a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion; the emperor composed a poem, and the preface read:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan the emperor granted a banquet at Qujiang Pavilion and composed a poem whose preface read:

sentences.zh: 朕在位僅將十載，實賴忠賢左右，克致小康。

translations.literal: I have been on the throne for nearly ten years, and truly rely on loyal worthies at my side to bring about modest prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: I have been on the throne for nearly ten years, and it is through the loyal worthies at my side that modest prosperity has been achieved.

sentences.zh: 是以擇三令節，錫茲宴賞，俾大夫、卿士得同歡洽也。

translations.literal: Therefore I have chosen one of the three fine festivals and granted this banquet and reward, so that grand masters and ministers may share in the same joy and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have chosen one of the three great festivals and granted this banquet, so that ministers and officials may share in the same joy.

sentences.zh: 夫共其戚者同其休，有其初者貴其終，咨爾群僚，頒朕不暇，樂而能節，職思其憂，鹹若時則，庶乎理矣。

translations.literal: Those who share in sorrow share in joy; those who have a beginning value the end. I address you, my officials: though I distribute rewards without pause, rejoice yet be restrained, in office think of cares, all follow the season's norms—then perhaps order may be attained.
translations.idiomatic: Those who share sorrow should share joy; those who begin a task should value its completion. I address you, my officials: though I grant rewards without pause, rejoice yet show restraint, and in office keep your duties in mind. If all observe the season's proprieties, good order may yet be attained.

sentences.zh: 因重陽之會，聊示所懷。

translations.literal: On the occasion of the Double Ninth, I briefly express what is in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of the Double Ninth Festival, I briefly express what is in my heart.

sentences.zh: 早衣對庭燎，躬化勤意誠。

translations.literal: Rising early to robe myself before the court torches, I personally transform with diligent intent and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Rising early to robe myself before the court torches, I labor in person to transform the realm with sincere diligence.

sentences.zh: 時此萬樞暇，適與佳節並。

translations.literal: Now amid the myriad affairs I have leisure, which happens to coincide with the fine festival.
translations.idiomatic: Now, amid the myriad affairs of state, a moment of leisure coincides with this fine festival.

sentences.zh: 曲池絜寒流，芳菊舒金英。

translations.literal: The winding pool holds clear cold currents; fragrant chrysanthemums unfold their golden blooms.
translations.idiomatic: The winding pool holds clear cold currents; fragrant chrysanthemums unfold their golden blooms.

sentences.zh: 乾坤爽氣澄，臺殿秋光清。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are clear with crisp air; terraces and halls shine with autumn light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are clear with crisp air; terraces and halls shine with autumn light.

sentences.zh: 朝野慶年豐，高會多歡聲。

translations.literal: Court and countryside rejoice in a bountiful year; at this lofty gathering many sounds of joy arise.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside rejoice in a bountiful year; at this lofty gathering many sounds of joy arise.

sentences.zh: 永懷無荒誡，良士同斯情。

translations.literal: Forever keeping in mind the warning against excess, good men share this feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Forever keeping in mind the warning against excess, good men share this feeling.

sentences.zh: 因詔曰：「卿等重陽會宴，朕想歡洽，欣慰良多，情發於中，因制詩序。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict said, "At your Double Ninth gathering I think of the joy and harmony and am greatly comforted; feeling arose within me, and therefore I composed this poem and preface."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "At your Double Ninth gathering I think of the joy we shared and am greatly comforted. Feeling arose within me, and therefore I composed this poem and preface."

sentences.zh: 今賜卿等一本，可中書門下簡定文詞士三五十人應制，同用『清』字，明日內於延英門進來。

translations.literal: Now I grant each of you a copy; the Secretariat may select thirty or fifty literary men to compose matching pieces, all using the rhyme word 'clear,' and submit them at the Yanying Gate by tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I now grant each of you a copy. The Secretariat may select thirty or fifty literary men to compose matching pieces, all using the rhyme word 'clear,' and submit them at the Yanying Gate by tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣李泌等雖奉詔簡擇，難於取舍，由是百僚皆和。

translations.literal: Chief ministers such as Li Bi, though ordered to select, found it hard to choose, and therefore all the officials composed matching pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers such as Li Bi, though ordered to make a selection, found it hard to choose among the candidates, and so all the officials composed matching pieces.

sentences.zh: 上自考其詩，以太真及李紓等四人為上等，鮑防、于邵等四人為次等，張濛、殷亮等二十三人為下等；

translations.literal: The emperor himself graded the poems, placing Taizhen and Li Shu and three others in the top grade, Bao Fang and Yu Shao and two others in the second grade, and Zhang Meng, Yin Liang, and twenty-one others in the lowest grade;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself graded the poems, placing Liu Taizhen, Li Shu, and two others in the top grade; Bao Fang, Yu Shao, and two others in the second; and Zhang Meng, Yin Liang, and twenty-one others in the lowest.

sentences.zh: 而李晟、馬燧、李泌三宰相之詩，不加考第。

translations.literal: but the poems of the three chief ministers Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Li Bi were not graded.
translations.idiomatic: The poems of the three chief ministers Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Li Bi were not graded.

sentences.zh: 初，硃泚、懷光之亂，關輔薦饑，貞元三年以後，仍歲豐稔，人始復生人之樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the disorders of Zhu Ci and Li Huaiguang, the Guanzhong region suffered repeated famine; after the third year of Zhenyuan, year after year brought rich harvests, and people began again to know the joys of life.
translations.idiomatic: After the disorders of Zhu Ci and Li Huaiguang, the Guanzhong region had suffered repeated famine. From the third year of Zhenyuan onward, harvests were abundant year after year, and people began again to know the ordinary joys of life.

sentences.zh: 德宗詔曰：「比者卿士內外，朝夕公務，今方隅無事，蒸民小康，其正月晦日、三月三日、九月九日三節日，宜任文武百僚擇勝地追賞。

translations.literal: Dezong issued an edict: "Lately civil and military officials within and without have been occupied day and night with public business; now the regions are at peace and the people enjoy modest prosperity. On the last day of the first month, the third day of the third month, and the ninth day of the ninth month—these three festivals—civil and military officials should be permitted to choose fine places for outings and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong issued an edict: "Lately officials within and without the capital have been occupied day and night with public business. Now the realm is at peace and the people enjoy modest prosperity. On the last day of the first month, the third day of the third month, and the ninth day of the ninth month—these three festivals—civil and military officials may choose fine places for outings and rewards."

sentences.zh: 每節宰相、常參官共賜錢五百貫文、翰林學士一百貫文，左右神威、神策等十軍各賜五百貫。

translations.literal: Each festival the chief ministers and regular attendees at court were together granted five hundred strings of cash, Hanlin academicians one hundred strings, and each of the ten armies including the Left and Right Divine Valor and Divine Strategy five hundred strings.
translations.idiomatic: Each festival the chief ministers and regular attendees at court were granted five hundred strings of cash together, Hanlin academicians one hundred strings, and each of the ten armies—including the Left and Right Divine Valor and Divine Strategy—five hundred strings.

sentences.zh: 金吾英武、威遠及諸衛將軍共賜二百貫，客省奏事共賜一百貫，委度支每節前五日支付，永為常制。

translations.literal: The generals of the Gold Crow, Valiant Martial, Far-reaching Prestige, and the various guards were together granted two hundred strings; those who presented memorials at the Guest Office one hundred strings; payment was entrusted to the Department of Public Works five days before each festival, to be a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The generals of the Gold Crow, Valiant Martial, Far-reaching Prestige, and the various guard units were granted two hundred strings together; those who presented memorials at the Guest Office one hundred strings. The Department of Public Works was to pay these sums five days before each festival, as a permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 」李紓李紓，字仲舒，禮部侍郎希言之子。

translations.literal: Li Shu, styled Zhongshu, was the son of Vice Minister of Rites Li Xiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu, whose courtesy name was Zhongshu, was the son of Vice Minister of Rites Li Xiyan.

sentences.zh: 少有文學。

translations.literal: From youth he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，拜秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era he was appointed collator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he was appointed collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，吏部侍郎李季卿薦為左補闕，累遷司封員外郎、知制誥，改中書舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Dali, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Remonstrator; he was successively promoted to vice director of the Department of Honors, put in charge of drafting edicts, and changed to drafting secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Jiqing recommended him as Left Remonstrator. He rose to vice director of the Department of Honors, took charge of drafting edicts, and was then appointed drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋自虢州刺史征拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned from prefect of Guo Prefecture and appointed vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned from his post as prefect of Guo Prefecture and appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，擇為同州刺史，尋棄州詣梁州行在，拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, Shu was chosen as prefect of Tong Prefecture; soon he abandoned the prefecture and went to the mobile court at Liangzhou, and was appointed vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, Li Shu was appointed prefect of Tong Prefecture. He soon abandoned his post and went to the mobile court at Liangzhou, where he was appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 反正，兼知選事。

translations.literal: After the restoration he was additionally put in charge of selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration he was additionally placed in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 李懷光誅，河東節度及諸軍會河中，詔往宣勞節度，使還，敷奏合旨，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Li Huaiguang was executed, the military commissioner of Hedong and the various armies assembled at Hezhong; an edict sent Shu to announce imperial favor to the armies; on his return his memorials suited the emperor's intent, and he was appointed vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Huaiguang was executed, the military commissioner of Hedong and the various armies assembled at Hezhong. Li Shu was sent to announce imperial favor to the troops. On his return his memorials pleased the emperor, and he was appointed vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 紓通達，善詼諧，好接後進，厚自奉養，鮮華輿馬，以放達蘊藉稱。

translations.literal: Shu was open-minded, skilled in wit and humor, fond of receiving younger talents, lavish in his own upkeep, with splendid carriages and horses, and was known for free-spirited refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu was open-minded and skilled in wit, fond of mentoring younger talents, lavish in his personal style, with splendid carriages and horses, and was known for free-spirited refinement.

sentences.zh: 雖為大官，而佚遊佐宴，不嘗自忘。

translations.literal: Though a high official, he still wandered freely and assisted at banquets, never forgetting himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though a high official, he still wandered freely and joined banquets as before, never putting on airs.

sentences.zh: 嘗議享武成王不當視文宣廟，奏云：「準開元十九年敕，置齊太公廟，以張良配，太常卿及少卿、丞充三獻官。

translations.literal: He once argued that sacrifices to the Martial Completion King should not be treated like those at the Temple of Literary Propagation, memorializing, "According to the edict of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, a temple to Duke Tai of Qi was established with Zhang Liang as associate; the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the vice directors and assistants served as the three offering officers."
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that sacrifices to the Martial Completion King should not be treated like those at the Temple of Literary Propagation, memorializing, "According to the edict of the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan, a temple to Duke Tai of Qi was established with Zhang Liang as associate; the director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and his deputies served as the three offering officers."

sentences.zh: 又按《開元禮》祝文雲『皇帝遣某官昭告於齊太公、漢留侯』。

translations.literal: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, the prayer text reads, 'The emperor sends a certain official to announce to Duke Tai of Qi and the Marquis of Liu of Han.'"
translations.idiomatic: According to the Kaiyuan Rites, the prayer text reads, 'The emperor sends a certain official to announce to Duke Tai of Qi and the Marquis of Liu of Han.'"

sentences.zh: 至上元年，敕追贈太公為武成王，享祭之典，一同文宣王，有司因差太尉充獻官，兼禦署祝板。

translations.literal: By the first year of Shangyuan an edict posthumously ennobled Duke Tai as Martial Completion King, and the sacrificial rites were made identical to those of the Literary Propagation King; the authorities therefore assigned the Grand Marshal as offering officer and also had him sign the prayer board.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shangyuan an edict posthumously ennobled Duke Tai as Martial Completion King, and the sacrificial rites were made identical to those of the Literary Propagation King. The authorities therefore assigned the Grand Marshal as offering officer and had him sign the prayer board.

sentences.zh: 伏以太公即周之太師，張良即漢之少傅，聖朝列於祀典，已極褒崇；

translations.literal: I submit that Duke Tai was Grand Tutor of Zhou and Zhang Liang was Junior Tutor of Han; our sage dynasty has placed them in the sacrificial canon and already accorded them the highest honor;
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Duke Tai was Grand Tutor of Zhou and Zhang Liang was Junior Tutor of Han. Our dynasty has placed them in the sacrificial canon and already accorded them the highest honor;

sentences.zh: 今屈禮於至尊，施敬於臣佐，理或過當，神何敢歆。

translations.literal: Now bending ritual before the Supreme Sovereign and bestowing reverence upon minister-assistants — the principle may exceed what is fitting; how would the spirits dare to accept it?
translations.idiomatic: To bend ritual before the Son of Heaven and pay the same reverence to mere ministers is, in principle, excessive; the spirits would scarcely dare receive such offerings.

sentences.zh: 伏以文宣垂教，百代宗師，五常三綱，非其訓不明，有國有家，非其制不立，故孟軻稱『生人已來，一人而已』。

translations.literal: I submit that Wencheng handed down teachings, the teacher of a hundred generations; the Five Constants and Three Bonds — without his instruction they would not be clear; state and family — without his institutions they would not stand. Thus Mencius said, 'Since men have lived, there has been only one man.'
translations.idiomatic: I submit that Confucius, styled Wencheng, handed down teachings and stands as the master of a hundred generations. The Five Constants and the Three Bonds would lack clarity without his instruction; no state or household could stand without his institutions. That is why Mencius said that since mankind began, there has been only one such man.

sentences.zh: 由是正素王之位，加先聖之名，樂用宮懸，獻差太尉，尊師崇道，雅合政經。

translations.literal: Hence he was given the position of uncrowned king in rectitude, honored with the title of First Sage; music employs the full palace bells, offering officers are appointed from the Grand Commandant — honoring the teacher and exalting the Way, elegantly accordant with statecraft and norms.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he was accorded the status of the uncrowned king, honored as the First Sage, granted the full palace orchestra, and assigned the Grand Commandant as offering officer — a fitting exaltation of the teacher and the Way, in keeping with the norms of governance.

sentences.zh: 且太公述作止於《六韜》，勛業形於一代，豈宜擬諸盛德，均其殊禮！

translations.literal: Moreover, the Grand Duke's writings extend only to the Six Strategies; his achievements took shape in a single age — how could he be compared to such surpassing virtue or granted equal extraordinary rites!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke's literary legacy is confined to the Six Strategies, and his achievements belong to a single age. How can he be ranked with such supreme virtue or granted the same extraordinary rites?

sentences.zh: 其祝文請不進署，『敢昭告』請改為『敬祭於』，『其昭告』請改為『致祭於留侯』，其獻官請準舊式，差太常卿已下充。

translations.literal: As for the prayer text, please do not submit it for imperial endorsement; change 'I dare announce' to 'I respectfully offer sacrifice to'; change 'announce to' to 'perform sacrifice to Marquis Liu'; for offering officers, please follow the old form, appointing the Grand Master of Ceremonies and those below.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer text should not be submitted for the emperor's signature. 'I dare announce' should read 'I respectfully offer sacrifice to,' and 'announce to' should read 'perform sacrifice to Marquis Liu.' Offering officers should follow the former practice, with the Grand Master of Ceremonies and his subordinates serving in that capacity.

sentences.zh: 」詔百僚進議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to advance proposals for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all officials to submit their opinions.

sentences.zh: 文武官上言，互有異同。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials submitted memorials, each disagreeing with the others.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials submitted memorials, voicing conflicting views.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「帝德廣運，乃武乃文，文化武功，皇王之二柄，祀禮教敬，國章孔明。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'The emperor's virtue is far-reaching; he is both martial and literary. Civil culture and martial achievement are the two handles of emperors and kings; sacrifice, rites, and teaching reverence are the clear standards of state regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'The emperor's virtue is far-reaching, encompassing both civil and martial excellence. Culture and military achievement are the twin pillars of kingship; sacrifices, rites, and the teaching of reverence are the clear norms of state governance.

sentences.zh: 自今宜上將軍以下充獻官，余依紓所奏。

translations.literal: From now on the Grand General of the Upper Army and those below should serve as offering officers; the rest follows what Shu memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the Grand General of the Upper Army and those of lower rank shall serve as offering officers; the remainder follows Li Shu's memorial.

sentences.zh: 」紓又奏詔為《興元紀功述》及郊廟樂章，諸所論著甚眾。

translations.literal: Shu again drafted edicts such as the Record of Achievements at Xingyuan and suburban and temple hymn texts; his writings were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shu also drafted edicts including the Record of Achievements at Xingyuan and suburban and temple hymn texts; his literary output was extensive.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died in office at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan (792) he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 邵說邵說，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Shao Yue. Shao Yue was a native of Anyang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yue. Shao Yue was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為史思明判官，歷事思明、朝義，常掌兵事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial officer under Shi Siming; he served Siming and Chaoyi and constantly managed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as aide to Shi Siming, remaining under Siming and his son Chaoyi and regularly handling military affairs.

sentences.zh: 朝義之敗，說降於軍前，郭子儀愛其才，留於幕下。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated, Yue surrendered before the army; Guo Ziyi valued his talent and kept him on staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaoyi was defeated, Yue surrendered to the imperial forces; Guo Ziyi admired his ability and retained him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 累授長安令、秘書少監，遷吏部侍郎、太子詹事，以才幹稱。

translations.literal: He was successively appointed magistrate of Chang'an, junior director of the Secretariat, promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and tutor to the crown prince, and was known for talent and competence.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as magistrate of Chang'an, junior director of the Secretariat, vice minister of Personnel, and crown prince tutor, and was recognized for his administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 談者或以宰相許之，金吾將軍裴儆謂諫議大夫柳載曰：「以鄙夫所度，說得禍不久矣。

translations.literal: Discussants sometimes promised him the chancellorship. General of the Golden Guards Pei Jing said to Remonstrance Adviser Liu Zai: 'By this humble man's estimate, Yue will soon meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Some spoke of him as future chancellor material. General of the Golden Guards Pei Jing said to Remonstrance Adviser Liu Zai: 'In my humble judgment, Yue will soon come to ruin.

sentences.zh: 且說與史思明父子定君臣之分，居劇官，掌兵柄，亡軀犯順，前後百戰，於賊庭掠名家子女以為婢仆者數十人，剽盜寶貨，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Moreover Yue with Shi Siming father and son established lord-and-minister distinctions, held weighty office, grasped military authority, risked body and violated obedience, fought in battle a hundred times back and forth, in the rebels' court seized famous families' sons and daughters to serve as maids and attendants numbering dozens, plundered treasures and goods beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yue had established a formal lord-and-minister relationship with Shi Siming and his son, held high office under them, wielded military command, and fought fiercely for the rebel cause in a hundred engagements. In the rebel camp he seized dozens of sons and daughters of eminent families as servants and plundered treasures beyond count.

sentences.zh: 力屈然後降，朝廷宥以不死。

translations.literal: Only when strength was exhausted did he surrender; the court pardoned him so he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered only when utterly defeated, and the court spared his life.

sentences.zh: 獲齒班序，無厚顏，而又遑遑求財，崇飾第宅，附托貴幸，以求大用，不知愧懼，而有得色，其能久乎！

translations.literal: He obtained a place in court ranks yet lacked thick face; moreover he hurried to seek wealth, gloriously adorned his residence, relied on the powerful and favored to seek great employment, knew no shame or fear yet had a look of satisfaction — can he last long!
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed back into court rank without shame, yet he aggressively sought wealth, lavishly furnished his residence, cultivated connections with powerful favorites to advance himself, showed no remorse or fear, and even looked pleased with himself — how could such a man endure!

sentences.zh: 」建中三年，嚴郢得罪，說與郢厚善，勸硃泚抗疏申其冤，說為草其奏，上知之，貶說歸州刺史，竟卒於貶所。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong Yan Ling offended; Yue was deeply friendly with Ling and urged Zhu Ci to submit a bold memorial stating his injustice; Yue drafted the memorial for him; the emperor learned of it and demoted Yue to prefect of Guizhou; he finally died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong (782) Yan Ling fell from favor. Yue was on close terms with Ling and urged Zhu Ci to submit a bold memorial in his defense; Yue drafted the document. When the emperor learned of it, Yue was demoted to prefect of Guizhou and ultimately died in exile.

sentences.zh: 于邵于邵，字相門，其先家於代，今為京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Yu Shao. Yu Shao, style name Xiangmen, his ancestors' home was in Dai, now registered as a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao. Yu Shao, styled Xiangmen, was descended from a family of Dai but was now registered in Wannian, Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖筠，戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yun was Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yun served as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 邵天寶末進士登科，書判超絕，授崇文館校書郎。

translations.literal: Shao at the end of Tianbao passed the jinshi examination with exceptional letter-judgment scores, appointed collation officer of the Chongwen Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shao passed the jinshi examination late in the Tianbao era with outstanding examination essays and was appointed a collation officer at the Chongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 累歷使府，入為起居郎，再遷比部郎中，尚二十考第於吏部，以當稱。

translations.literal: He successively served in commissioners' offices, entered as court diarist, was twice promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue, still lacked twenty years of evaluations ranked at the Ministry of Personnel, and was deemed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He served in several provincial staffs before entering the capital as court diarist and rising twice to director in the Ministry of Revenue. Though he had not yet completed twenty years of personnel evaluations, he was judged fully qualified.

sentences.zh: 無何，出為道州刺史，未就道，轉巴州。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of Daozhou; before taking up the post he was transferred to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed prefect of Daozhou but was reassigned to Bazhou before departing.

sentences.zh: 時歲儉，夷獠數千相聚山澤，圍州掠眾，邵勵州兵以拒之。

translations.literal: At the time the year was lean; several thousand Yi and Liao gathered in mountains and marshes, besieged the prefecture and plundered the people; Shao encouraged the prefectural troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the region, and several thousand tribal forces gathered in the hills and marshes, besieging the prefecture and raiding the populace. Shao rallied the prefectural troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 旬有二日，遣使說喻，盜邀邵面降，邵儒服出城，盜羅拜而降，圍解，節度使李抱玉以聞，超遷梓州，以疾不至，遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: After twelve days he sent envoys to persuade them; the bandits invited Shao to face them and surrender; Shao in scholar's dress went out of the city; the bandits lined up bowing and surrendered; the siege was lifted; military commissioner Li Baoyu reported it; he was exceptionally promoted to Zizhou but did not arrive due to illness; transferred to director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After twelve days he sent envoys to negotiate. The insurgents demanded that Shao appear in person to accept their surrender. Dressed in scholarly robes, he went outside the city walls, where the rebels lined up and prostrated themselves. The siege was lifted. Military commissioner Li Baoyu reported the achievement, and Shao was exceptionally promoted to Zizhou, though illness prevented him from taking up the post; he was then appointed director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使崔寧請留為支度副使。

translations.literal: Military commissioner of Xichuan Cui Ning requested he remain as deputy commissioner for revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, military commissioner of Xichuan, asked that he remain as deputy commissioner for logistics.

sentences.zh: 尋拜諫議大夫、知制誥，再遷禮部侍郎、史館修撰，為三司使。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Remonstrance Adviser and drafter of edicts, twice promoted to vice minister of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute, made commissioner of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Remonstrance Adviser and drafter of edicts, then twice promoted to vice minister of Rites and compiler at the Historiography Institute, and made commissioner of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 以撰上尊號冊，賜階三品，當時大詔令，皆出於邵。

translations.literal: For composing the book of supreme honorific titles he was granted third rank; at the time major edicts all issued from Shao.
translations.idiomatic: For drafting the text conferring an honorific title upon the emperor, he was granted third rank. All major edicts of the period were composed by Shao.

sentences.zh: 頃之，與御史中丞袁高、給事中蔣鎮雜理左丞薛邕詔獄。

translations.literal: Before long, together with Censor-in-chief Yuan Gao and Secretariat Drafter Jiang Zhen he jointly handled the edict-case of Left Vice Director Xue Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he joined Censor-in-chief Yuan Gao and Secretariat Recipient Jiang Zhen in investigating the edict-case against Left Vice Director Xue Yong.

sentences.zh: 邵以為邕犯在赦前，奏出之，失旨，貶桂州長史。

translations.literal: Shao held that Yong's offense was before the amnesty and memorialized to release him; he missed the emperor's intent and was demoted to chief administrator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shao argued that Yong's offense predated the amnesty and memorialized for his release. This displeased the emperor, and Shao was demoted to chief administrator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，除原王傅，後為太子賓客，與宰相陸贄不睦。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Yuan; later made crown prince's attendant; he was not on good terms with chancellor Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Yuan and later crown prince attendant. He was on poor terms with Chancellor Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為杭州刺史，以疾請告，坐貶衢州別駕，移江州別駕，卒年八十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as prefect of Hangzhou; on illness he requested leave; punished and demoted to vice prefect of Quzhou; moved to vice prefect of Jiangzhou; died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (792) he was sent out as prefect of Hangzhou. When he requested leave on grounds of illness, he was demoted to vice prefect of Quzhou, then transferred to vice prefect of Jiangzhou, and died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 邵性孝悌，內行修潔，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Shao's nature was filial and fraternal; his inner conduct was cultivated and pure, and in old age he became even more devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was filial and dutiful, exemplary in private conduct, and became even more devoted in his later years.

sentences.zh: 初，樊澤常舉賢良方正，邵一見之於京師，曰：「將相之材也。

translations.literal: Early on Fan Ze regularly submitted for Worthy and Direct categories; Shao on seeing him once in the capital said, 'Material for general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career Fan Ze submitted for the Worthy and Direct examination. When Shao met him in the capital, he declared, 'This man has the makings of a general or minister.

sentences.zh: 」不十五年，澤為節將。

translations.literal: Within less than fifteen years, Ze became a frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Within fifteen years Fan Ze had become a military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰年近五十，始舉進士，邵異其文，擢第甲科，且曰：「不十五年，當掌詔令。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanhan was nearly fifty when he first submitted for jinshi; Shao marveled at his writing, advanced him to first class in the examination, and said, 'Within fifteen years he will control edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan was nearly fifty when he first took the jinshi examination. Shao was struck by his literary talent and advanced him to the top class, declaring, 'Within fifteen years he will draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 」竟如其言。

translations.literal: It ended just as he said.
translations.idiomatic: The prediction proved exactly right.

sentences.zh: 獨孤授舉博學宏詞，吏部考為乙第，在中書覆升甲科，人稱其當。

translations.literal: Dugu Shou submitted for Erudite Learning and Grand Composition; the Ministry of Personnel graded him second class; at the Secretariat review he was raised to first class; people said it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Shou submitted for the Erudite Learning and Grand Composition examination and was initially placed in the second class by the Ministry of Personnel, but on review at the Secretariat was raised to the first class — a judgment widely regarded as fair.

sentences.zh: 有集四十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to forty juan.

sentences.zh: 崔元翰崔元翰者，博陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Yuanhan. Cui Yuanhan was a man of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanhan. Cui Yuanhan was a native of Boling.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第，登博學宏詞制科，又應賢良方正、直言極諫科，三舉皆升甲第，年已五十余。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination, passed the Erudite Learning and Grand Composition regulated subject, also responded to Worthy and Direct and Outspoken Remonstrance extreme subjects; all three submissions rose to first class; he was already over fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and the Erudite Learning and Grand Composition examination, and also submitted to the Worthy and Direct and Outspoken Remonstrance subjects — all three at the top level — by which time he was already over fifty.

sentences.zh: 李汧公鎮滑臺，辟為從事。

translations.literal: Duke of Fen garrisoned Huatai and recruited him as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaizhong, Duke of Fen, held Huatai, he recruited Yuanhan as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 後北平王馬燧在太原，聞其名，致禮命之，又為燧府掌書記。

translations.literal: Later Prince of Beiping Ma Sui was at Taiyuan, heard his name, sent ritual courtesy to summon him, and he again served as Sui's headquarters registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ma Sui, Prince of Beiping, was at Taiyuan, he heard of Yuanhan's reputation, sent ceremonial invitation, and appointed him registrar on his staff.

sentences.zh: 入朝為太常博士、禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and outer section member of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court service as academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and outer-section member of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 竇參輔政，用為知制誥，詔令溫雅，合於典謨。

translations.literal: Dou Can assisted government and used him as drafter of edicts; his edicts were mild and elegant, fitting the classics and counsels.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Can served as chief minister, Yuanhan was appointed drafter of edicts; his drafts were refined and elegant, in keeping with classical models.

sentences.zh: 然性太剛褊簡傲，不能取容於時，每發言論，略無阿徇，忤執政旨，故掌誥二年，而官不遷。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was too rigid, narrow, plain, and proud; he could not win accommodation of the age; whenever he voiced opinions he had little flattery or compliance, offended the ruling intent; therefore though he handled edicts for two years his office did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his disposition was excessively rigid, blunt, and proud; he could not adapt to his times and invariably spoke his mind without deference, offending those in power. Though he drafted edicts for two years, he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 竟罷知制誥，守比部郎中。

translations.literal: In the end he was removed from drafting edicts and kept the post of director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually removed from edict drafting and retained only his post as director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 元翰苦心文章，時年七十余，好學不倦。

translations.literal: Yuanhan toiled at literary craft; at the time he was over seventy, loving learning without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan devoted himself tirelessly to literary craft. Even past seventy he pursued learning without cease.

sentences.zh: 既介獨耿直，故少交遊，唯秉一操，伏膺翰墨。

translations.literal: Since he was independent and uprightly honest, he had few associations; he held to one principle alone and applied himself to brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Independent and upright by nature, he had few social ties and devoted himself single-mindedly to literature.

sentences.zh: 其對策及奏記、碑誌、師法班固、蔡伯喈，而致思精密。

translations.literal: His policy essays, memorials, inscriptions, and epitaphs took Ban Gu and Cai Yong as models, with finely wrought thought.
translations.idiomatic: His examination essays, memorials, inscriptions, and epitaphs followed the models of Ban Gu and Cai Yong, marked by meticulous craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 為時所擯，終於散位。

translations.literal: Rejected by the age, he ended in office without substantive duties.
translations.idiomatic: Rejected by his contemporaries, he ended his career in a nominal post without substantive duties.

sentences.zh: 于公異于公異者，吳人。

translations.literal: Yu Gongyi. Yu Gongyi was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gongyi. Yu Gongyi was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，文章精拔，為時所稱。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi rank; his compositions were keen and outstanding, praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination; his writings were excellent and widely praised.

sentences.zh: 建中末，為李晟招討府掌書記。

translations.literal: Late in Jianzhong he was registrar of Li Sheng's Pacification Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianzhong era he served as registrar on Li Sheng's pacification staff.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，收京城，公異為露布上行在云：「臣已肅清宮禁，祗奏寢園，鐘虡不移，廟貌如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan the capital was recovered; Gongyi composed a battlefield report sent up while the emperor was still on campaign: 'Your subject has already made pure the palace enclosure, reverently announced the imperial tombs; bells and ritual stands have not moved; temple appearance is as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan (784), when the capital was recovered, Gongyi drafted a battlefield dispatch to the emperor still on campaign: 'Your servant has restored order within the palace precincts and reverently reported on the imperial tombs. The ritual bells remain in place, and the temple halls are intact.

sentences.zh: 」德宗覽之，泣下不自勝，左右為之嗚咽。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong on reading it wept beyond control; those at his side sobbed for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong read it he wept uncontrollably, and those around him wept as well.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「不知誰為之？

translations.literal: Presently he said, 'I do not know who wrote it?
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, 'Who wrote this?

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「于公異之詞也。

translations.literal: Someone replied, 'It is Yu Gongyi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Someone replied, 'It was written by Yu Gongyi.

sentences.zh: 」上稱善久之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it at length.

sentences.zh: 公異初應進士時，與舉人陸贄不協；

translations.literal: When Gongyi first responded to jinshi he was not in harmony with examinee Lu Zhi;
translations.idiomatic: When Gongyi first took the jinshi examination, he was on poor terms with fellow candidate Lu Zhi;

sentences.zh: 至是贄為翰林學士，聞上稱與，尤不悅。

translations.literal: by now Zhi was Hanlin academician; hearing the emperor's praise of him, he was especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: by now Lu Zhi was a Hanlin academician and was especially displeased to hear the emperor's praise.

sentences.zh: 時議者言之，公異少時不為後母所容，自遊宦成名，不歸鄉里；

translations.literal: Discussants of the time spoke of it: Gongyi in youth was not tolerated by his stepmother; since gaining fame through official travel he did not return to his native place;
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries noted that Gongyi's stepmother had rejected him in youth and that, once he rose to prominence through official service, he never returned home;

sentences.zh: 及貞元中陸贄為宰相，奏公異無素行，黜之。

translations.literal: when in Zhenyuan Lu Zhi was chancellor he memorialized that Gongyi lacked proper conduct and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: and when Lu Zhi became chancellor in the Zhenyuan era, he memorialized that Gongyi lacked proper moral conduct and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「祠部員外郎于公異，頃以才名，升於省闥。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Outer-section member of the Ministry of Rites Yu Gongyi, recently by talent and name rose within the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'Yu Gongyi, outer-section member of the Ministry of Rites, has recently risen within the ministries on the strength of his talent and reputation.

sentences.zh: 其少也，為父母之所不容，宜其引慝在躬，孝行不匱，匿名跡於畎畝，候安否於門閭，俾其親之過不彰，庶其誠之至必感。

translations.literal: In his youth he was not tolerated by his parents; he ought to harbor shame in person and not exhaust filial conduct, hide name and traces in fields, watch for their well-being at the gate, let his parents' faults not be displayed, perhaps his utmost sincerity would surely move them.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was rejected by his parents. He ought to have borne his failings inwardly and devoted himself to filial duty, living obscurely in the countryside while watching over his parents' welfare at their doorstep, concealing their wrongs and hoping that utmost sincerity might move them.

sentences.zh: 安於棄斥，遊學遠方，忘其溫凊之戀，竟至存亡之隔，為人子者，忍至是乎！

translations.literal: Content in abandonment and rejection, he wandered studying in far regions, forgot his longing for their warmth and coolness, finally reaching the separation of life and death — as a son of man, can one bear to this point!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was content with exile, traveled far to study, forgot his duty to inquire after their comfort, and ultimately allowed the barrier between life and death to go unbridged. What son could endure to such a point!

sentences.zh: 宜放歸田里，俾自循省。

translations.literal: He should be released to fields and village to make himself reflect.
translations.idiomatic: He should be sent back to his home village to reflect on his conduct.

sentences.zh: 其舉公異官尚書左丞盧邁，宜奪俸兩月。

translations.literal: The one who promoted Gongyi's office, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Mai, should have salary seized for two months.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mai, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, who had recommended Gongyi, should forfeit two months' salary.

sentences.zh: 」時中書舍人高郢薦監察御史元敦義，及睹公異譴逐，懼為所累，乃上疏首陳敦義虧於禮教，詔嘉郢之知過，俾敦義罷歸。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Drafter Gao Ying recommended Investigating Censor Yuan Dunyi; on seeing Gongyi's punishment and dismissal, fearing to be implicated, he submitted a memorial first stating Dunyi's failure in ritual teaching; an edict praised Ying's knowledge of fault and made Dunyi retire.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Secretariat Drafter Gao Ying had recommended Investigating Censor Yuan Dunyi. Seeing Gongyi punished, Ying feared implication and preemptively memorialized that Dunyi had failed in ritual conduct. The edict praised Ying's self-awareness and ordered Dunyi to return home.

sentences.zh: 公異竟名位不振，感軻而卒，人士惜其才，惡贄之褊急焉。

translations.literal: Gongyi in the end did not flourish in name or position; moved by indignation he died; gentlemen regretted his talent and detested Zhi's narrow impatience.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi never regained standing, died of grief, and scholars regretted his talent while condemning Lu Zhi's narrow vindictiveness.

sentences.zh: 呂渭呂渭，字君載，河中人。

translations.literal: Lu Wei. Lu Wei, style Junzai, a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wei. Lu Wei, styled Junzai, was a native of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父延之，越州刺史、浙江東道節度使。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was prefect of Yuezhou and military commissioner of Zhedong East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi served as prefect of Yue and military commissioner of Zhedong East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 渭舉進士，累授婺州永康令、大理評事。

translations.literal: Wei passed jinshi, was successively appointed magistrate of Yongkang in Wuzhou, and evaluating official of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed the jinshi examination and served successively as magistrate of Yongkang in Wu Prefecture and evaluating official of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李涵辟為支使，再遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Han recruited him as revenue aide; twice promoted to palace attending censor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, observation commissioner of Zhexi, recruited him as staff officer, and he was twice promoted to palace attending censor.

sentences.zh: 涵自御史大夫改太子少傅，渭上言：「涵父名少康，今涵為少傅，恐乖朝典。

translations.literal: Han from Censor-in-chief was changed to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Wei submitted memorial: 'Han's father's name is Shaokang; now Han is Junior Tutor — I fear it violates court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was transferred from Censor-in-chief to junior tutor of the heir apparent, Wei memorialized: 'Han's father's given name was Shaokang. For Han to become junior tutor (shaofu) may violate court taboo regulations.

sentences.zh: 」由是特授渭司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Because of this Wei was specially appointed outer-section member of the Department of Gatekeeping.
translations.idiomatic: For this Wei was specially appointed outer-section member of the Department of Gatekeeping.

sentences.zh: 尋為御史臺劾奏：「涵再任少卿，此時都不言；

translations.literal: Soon the Censorate impeached and memorialized: 'Han twice held vice director — at those times he said nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Censorate impeached him, noting: 'When Han twice held vice-director posts he said nothing of this;

sentences.zh: 今為少傅，疑以散慢，乃為不可。

translations.literal: now as Junior Tutor, suspected of being lax and disrespectful, it is therefore improper.
translations.idiomatic: now as junior tutor he raises the issue only from laxness and disrespect — this is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 」由是貶渭歙州司馬，改涵檢校工部尚書、兼光祿卿。

translations.literal: Because of this Wei was demoted to militia adjutant of Shezhou; Han was changed to checking Minister of Works and concurrently Director of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was therefore demoted to militia adjutant of She Prefecture, while Han was reassigned as acting Minister of Works with concurrent duties as Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 渭累授舒州刺史、吏部員外、駕部郎中、知制詔、中書舍人，母憂罷。

translations.literal: Wei was successively appointed prefect of Shuzhou, outer-section member of Personnel, director in the Ministry of Carriages, drafter of edicts, Secretariat Drafter — on mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei served successively as prefect of Shu, outer-section member of Personnel, director in the Ministry of Carriages, drafter of edicts, and Secretariat Drafter before leaving office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授太子右庶子、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Right Vice Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed right vice supervisor of the heir apparent and vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 中書省有柳樹，建中末枯死，興元元年車駕還京後，其樹再榮，人謂之瑞柳。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there was a willow tree; late Jianzhong it withered and died; in first year of Xingyuan after the imperial carriage returned to the capital the tree flourished again; people called it the auspicious willow.
translations.idiomatic: A willow tree stood in the Secretariat compound. It had died at the end of the Jianzhong era, but after the emperor's return to the capital in the first year of Xingyuan (784) it flourished again, and people called it the auspicious willow.

sentences.zh: 渭試進士，取瑞柳為賦題，上聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Wei when testing jinshi candidates took the auspicious willow as fu topic; the emperor heard and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei supervised the jinshi examination he set the auspicious willow as the composition topic, which the emperor commended.

sentences.zh: 渭又結附裴延齡之子操，舉進士，文詞非工，渭擢之登第，為正人嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Wei also attached himself to Pei Yanling's son Cao; Cao submitted for jinshi; his literary wording was not skilled; Wei advanced him to pass the examination; upright men derided and despised it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also cultivated ties with Pei Yanling's son Cao, advancing him to jinshi status despite mediocre literary skill — to the scorn of upright officials.

sentences.zh: 因入閣遺失請托文記，遂出為潭州刺史、兼御史中丞、湖南都團練觀察使，在任三歲，政甚煩碎。

translations.literal: Because upon entering the council chamber he lost a written note of requests and favors, he was sent out as prefect of Tanzhou, concurrently Censor-in-chief and Hunan commander of united training and observation; in office three years his government was very cumbersome and petty.
translations.idiomatic: After losing a list of favor-seeking requests upon entering the imperial council chamber, he was sent out as prefect of Tan, concurrently censor-in-chief and Hunan military commissioner. During three years in office his administration was notably fussy and petty.

sentences.zh: 貞元十六年卒，年六十六，贈陜州大都督。

translations.literal: In sixteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at age sixty-six; posthumously appointed Grand Protector General of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan (800) at sixty-six and was posthumously appointed grand protector general of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子溫、恭、儉、讓。

translations.literal: Sons Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wen, Gong, Jian, and Rang.

sentences.zh: 子 溫溫，字化光，貞元末登進士第，與翰林學士韋執誼善。

translations.literal: Son Wen. Wen, style Huaguang, at end of Zhenyuan passed jinshi rank, was friendly with Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen. Wen, styled Huaguang, passed the jinshi examination late in the Zhenyuan era and became close to Hanlin academician Wei Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 順宗在東宮，侍書王叔文勸太子招納時之英俊以自輔，溫與執誼尤為叔文所睠，起家再命拜左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong was Eastern Palace heir, attendant scribe Wang Shuwen urged the crown prince to recruit the age's outstanding talents to assist himself; Wen and Zhiyi were especially favored by Shuwen; from first appointment twice ordered appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, attendant Wang Shuwen urged him to recruit outstanding talents as aides. Wen and Zhiyi were especially favored by Shuwen, and Wen was twice appointed directly to left remembrancer.

sentences.zh: 二十年冬，副工部侍郎張薦為入吐蕃使，行至鳳翔，轉侍御史，賜緋袍牙笏。

translations.literal: In winter of the twentieth year, deputy to Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian as envoy entering Tibet; reaching Fengxiang, transferred to attending censor, granted crimson robe and ivory tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twentieth year (804) he served as deputy to Vice Minister of Works Zhang Jian on an embassy to Tibet. Reaching Fengxiang, he was appointed attending censor and granted the crimson robe and ivory tablet of office.

sentences.zh: 明年，德宗晏駕，順宗即位，張薦卒於青海，吐蕃以中國喪禍，留溫經年。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Dezong passed away; Shunzong ascended; Zhang Jian died at Qinghai; Tibet used China's funeral calamity and detained Wen for a year.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Dezong died and Shunzong ascended the throne. Zhang Jian died in Qinghai, and the Tibetans, citing China's imperial mourning, detained Wen for a full year.

sentences.zh: 時王叔文用事，故與溫同遊東宮者，皆不次任用，溫在蕃中，悲嘆久之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shuwen held power; therefore those who with Wen had associated in the Eastern Palace were all appointed out of turn; Wen was in Tibet and sighed in grief for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen was then in power, and all who had associated with Wen in the Eastern Palace were rapidly promoted. Wen, stranded in Tibet, lamented at length.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，使還，轉戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: In first year of Yuanhe the embassy returned; transferred to outer-section member of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe (806) he returned from the embassy and was appointed outer-section member of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時柳宗元等九人坐叔文貶逐。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Zongyuan and nine others sat with Shuwen and were demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Zongyuan and eight others were banished for their association with Shuwen.

sentences.zh: 唯溫以奉使免。

translations.literal: Only Wen by virtue of diplomatic mission was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wen was exempted because of his diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 溫天才俊拔，文彩贍逸，為時流柳宗元、劉禹錫所稱。

translations.literal: Wen's heavenly talent was outstanding and elevated; literary coloring was rich and expansive; contemporaries Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen possessed brilliant talent and elegant literary style, praised by contemporaries such as Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 然性多險詐，好奇近利，與竇群、羊士諤趣尚相狎。

translations.literal: Yet his nature had much treachery and deceit, loved the curious and drew near profit, with Dou Qun and Yang Shie their tastes and pursuits were mutually familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was treacherous by nature, drawn to novelty and profit, and was on intimate terms with Dou Qun and Yang Shie.

sentences.zh: 群為韋夏卿所薦，自處士不數年至御史中丞，李吉甫尤奇待之。

translations.literal: Qun was recommended by Wei Xiaqing; from unaffiliated scholar within a few years to Vice Censor-in-Chief, Li Jiji especially regarded him with wonder and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Qun had been recommended by Wei Xiaqing; in only a few years he rose from unaffiliated scholar to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Li Jiji treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 三年，吉甫為中官所惡，將出鎮揚州，溫欲乘其有間傾之。
