translations.literal: In the third year, Jiji was hated by inner eunuchs and was about to go out to govern Yangzhou; Wen wished to seize an opening to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhe, Li Jiji incurred the hatred of palace eunuchs and was about to take up command at Yangzhou; Lü Wen meant to seize the chance to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 溫自司封員外郎轉刑部郎中，竇群請為知雜。

translations.literal: Wen transferred from Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments to Director in the Ministry of Justice; Dou Qun requested him as handler of miscellaneous censorate business.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen moved from Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments to Director in the Ministry of Justice, and Dou Qun had him appointed to handle miscellaneous censorate affairs.

sentences.zh: 吉甫以疾在第，召醫人陳登診視，夜宿於安邑裏第。

translations.literal: Jiji was ill at his residence; he summoned the physician Chen Deng to examine him, and Deng lodged overnight at the mansion in Anyi Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji lay ill at home and summoned the physician Chen Deng to examine him; Deng stayed the night at Jiji's mansion in Anyi Lane.

sentences.zh: 溫伺知之，詰旦，令吏捕登鞫問之，又奏劾吉甫交通術士。

translations.literal: Wen learned of it by spying; at dawn he ordered clerks to seize Deng and interrogate him under torture, and also memorialized impeaching Jiji for trafficking with occultists.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen learned of this through surveillance. At dawn he had his clerks seize Chen Deng and interrogate him under torture, and he also memorialized accusing Li Jiji of consorting with occult practitioners.

sentences.zh: 憲宗異之，召登面訊，其事皆虛，乃貶群為湖南觀察使，羊士諤資州刺史，溫均州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianzong thought it strange and summoned Deng to question him face to face; the matter was entirely false, and therefore Qun was demoted to Hunan Observation Commissioner, Yang Shi'e to Prefect of Zizhou, and Wen to Prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong found the affair suspicious and summoned Chen Deng for a personal inquiry; everything proved false. Dou Qun was therefore demoted to Hunan observation commissioner, Yang Shi'e to prefect of Zizhou, and Lü Wen to prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝議以所責太輕，群再貶黔南，溫貶道州刺史。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the penalties were too light; Qun was demoted again to Qiannan, and Wen to Prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that the punishments were too lenient; Dou Qun was demoted again to Qiannan, and Lü Wen to prefect of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉衡州，秩滿歸京，不得意，發疾卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hengzhou; when his term ended he returned to the capital, was discontented, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Hengzhou. When his term expired he returned to the capital, found no satisfaction there, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 溫文體富艷，有丘明、班固之風，所著《淩煙閣功臣銘》、《張始興畫贊》、《移博士書》，頗為文士所賞，有文集十卷。

translations.literal: Wen's literary style was rich and gorgeous, with the manner of Qiu Ming and Ban Gu; his compositions "Inscription on the Lingyan Pavilion Meritorious Ministers," "Encomium on Zhang Shixing's Painting," and "Letter Transferring the Erudites" were much prized by men of letters, and he had a collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wen's prose was sumptuous and brilliant, in the manner of Qiu Ming and Ban Gu. His "Inscription on the Meritorious Ministers of the Lingyan Pavilion," "Encomium on Zhang Shixing's Painting," and "Letter on Transferring the Erudites" won high praise among literary men, and he left collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子 恭、儉恭、儉皆至侍御史，讓至太子右庶子，皆有美才。

translations.literal: Sons Gong and Jian both reached Attendant Censor; Rang reached Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince—all possessed fine talent.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Gong and Jian both rose to attendant censor, and Rang to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince; all were men of notable ability.

sentences.zh: 自後吉甫再入中書，長慶以後，李德裕黨盛，呂氏諸子無至達官者。

translations.literal: Afterward Jiji again entered the Secretariat; after the Changqing era, when Li Deyu's faction flourished, none of the sons of the Lü clan reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Jiji again entered the Secretariat, but after the Changqing period, when Li Deyu's faction was ascendant, none of the Lü clan's sons attained high office.

sentences.zh: 鄭雲逵鄭雲逵，滎陽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yunkui was a man of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yunkui was a native of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，舉進士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性果誕敢言。

translations.literal: By nature he was decisive, bold, and outspoken.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was decisive, bold, and outspoken.

sentences.zh: 客遊兩河，以畫幹於硃泚，泚悅，乃表為節度掌書記、檢校祠部員外郎，仍以弟滔女妻之。

translations.literal: Traveling as a guest in the two He regions, he won Zhu Ci's favor through painting, and Ci was pleased; he therefore memorialized him as secretary on the military commission staff and Acting Vice Director in the Bureau of Sacrifices, and moreover gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in the two He regions he impressed Zhu Ci with his painting. Ci was delighted, memorialized him as secretary on the military commission staff and acting Vice Director in the Bureau of Sacrifices, and gave him Zhu Tao's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 泚將入覲，先令雲逵入奏；

translations.literal: When Ci was about to enter court audience, he first ordered Yunkui to go in and report.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was about to proceed to the capital for audience, he first sent Yunkui ahead to present his report.

sentences.zh: 及泚至京，以事怒雲逵，奏貶莫州參軍。

translations.literal: When Ci reached the capital, he took offense at Yunkui over some matter and memorialized his demotion to Army Adjutant of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Ci reached the capital he took offense at Yunkui over some affair and memorialized his demotion to army adjutant of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 滔代泚後，請為判官。

translations.literal: After Tao replaced Ci, he requested Yunkui as his secretarial aide.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Tao succeeded Zhu Ci, he asked to have Yunkui as his secretarial aide.

sentences.zh: 滔助田悅為逆，雲逵渝之不從，遂棄妻子馳歸長安，帝嘉其來，留於客省，超拜諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Tao aided Tian Yue in rebellion; Yunkui admonished him not to follow, then abandoned wife and children and galloped back to Chang'an; the emperor praised his coming, kept him in the Guest Bureau, and promoted him in one step to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao aided Tian Yue in rebellion, Yunkui urged him to desist and, when he would not, abandoned wife and children and rode posthaste to Chang'an. The emperor commended his return, lodged him in the Guest Bureau, and promoted him directly to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 奉天之難，雲逵奔赴行在，李晟以為行軍司馬，戎略多以咨之。

translations.literal: In the hardship at Fengtian, Yunkui hurried to the mobile court; Li Sheng made him Marching Army Marshal, and military strategy was often referred to him for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: During the crisis at Fengtian, Yunkui rushed to the emperor's mobile court. Li Sheng appointed him Marching Army Marshal and often consulted him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 歷秘書少監、給事中，尋拜大理卿，遷刑部、兵部二侍郎、遷御史中丞，充順宗山陵橋道置頓使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Palace Library and Supervising Secretary, soon was appointed Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of War, was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was appointed Commissioner for Bridge Routes and Staging Posts at Emperor Shunzong's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Vice Director of the Palace Library and Supervising Secretary, was soon made Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice and Vice Minister of War, then to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and was appointed commissioner for bridge routes and staging posts at Emperor Shunzong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雲逵初為硃泚判官，常忤同幕蔡庭玉；

translations.literal: Yunkui had first been Zhu Ci's secretarial aide and had often offended his colleague on the staff Cai Tingyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yunkui had first served as Zhu Ci's secretarial aide and had often clashed with his colleague on the staff, Cai Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 庭玉白泚，黜為莫州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Tingyu reported to Ci, and he was demoted to Recorder of Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tingyu reported him to Zhu Ci, and Yunkui was demoted to recorder of Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 滔復奏為判官，因深構庭玉於滔；

translations.literal: Tao again memorialized him as secretarial aide, and therefore deeply framed Tingyu before Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao again memorialized him as secretarial aide, and Yunkui thereupon worked hard to turn Tao against Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 滔為泚留後事，有請於泚，庭玉又輒隳之。

translations.literal: Tao, handling regent affairs while Ci was away, would make requests of Ci, and Tingyu would again repeatedly thwart them.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Tao acted as regent during Zhu Ci's absence, whenever he sought Ci's approval on some matter, Cai Tingyu would again and again obstruct it.

sentences.zh: 又有判官硃體微，亦蒙泚親信，與庭玉常從容言於泚曰：「滔非長者，不可付以兵權。

translations.literal: There was also secretarial aide Zhu Tiyi, who likewise enjoyed Ci's intimate trust; with Tingyu he would speak at leisure to Ci, saying, "Tao is no elder worth trusting—military authority must not be entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Another secretarial aide, Zhu Tiyi, also enjoyed Zhu Ci's intimate confidence; he and Tingyu would speak to Ci at leisure, saying, "Zhu Tao is no man of stature and must not be entrusted with military authority."

sentences.zh: 」滔竊知之。

translations.literal: Tao secretly learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao learned of this in secret.

sentences.zh: 後滔南討有功，雲逵數激怒之，滔乃抗表論庭玉等離間骨肉；

translations.literal: Later, when Tao campaigned south and won merit, Yunkui repeatedly provoked him; Tao then submitted a defiant memorial accusing Tingyu and the others of sowing discord between flesh and blood.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Zhu Tao's successful southern campaigns, Yunkui repeatedly goaded him; Tao then submitted a defiant memorial accusing Tingyu and the others of driving a wedge between kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 及滔叛，帝乃召泚以表示之，故歸罪於庭玉等以悅滔，滔亦終叛。

translations.literal: When Tao rebelled, the emperor then summoned Ci and showed him the memorial; therefore blame was laid on Tingyu and the others to please Tao, yet Tao ultimately rebelled all the same.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Tao rebelled, the emperor summoned Zhu Ci and showed him the memorial; blame was therefore placed on Tingyu and the others to placate Tao, yet Tao rebelled in the end nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 三年，雲逵奏：其弟前太仆丞方逵，「受性兇悖，不知君親，眾惡備身，訓教莫及，結聚兇黨，江中劫人。

translations.literal: In the third year Yunkui memorialized: his younger brother, former Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Fang Kui, "by nature is fierce and perverse, knows neither sovereign nor parent, all abomination is concentrated in his person, instruction and correction cannot reach him; he gathers violent factions and robs people on the Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yunkui memorialized concerning his younger brother, the former Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Fang Kui: "By nature he is savage and rebellious, heedless of sovereign and parent; universal hatred is fixed upon him, and no teaching can reform him. He gathers violent bands and robs travelers on the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 臣亡父先臣昈杖至一百，終不能斃。

translations.literal: My deceased father the late subject Hao beat him with the cane up to one hundred strokes, yet in the end could not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: My late father, the former subject Hao, beat him with the staff as many as a hundred times, yet could not bring him to his death.

sentences.zh: 張延賞任揚州日，亦曾犯延賞法，決殺復蘇。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yanzao held Yangzhou, he too once violated Yanzao's law; sentenced to execution, he revived afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanzao governed Yangzhou, Fang Kui likewise once violated his law; though sentenced to execution, he revived afterward.

sentences.zh: 至於常言，皆呼臣亡父先臣名，親戚所知，無可教語。

translations.literal: As for his constant talk, he always calls out my deceased father's personal name; kinsmen know this—there is nothing left to teach him.
translations.idiomatic: In his daily speech he constantly calls my late father by his personal name; our kinsmen know it—there is no further correcting him.

sentences.zh: 昨聞於邠、寧、慶等州幹謁節度及州縣乞丐，今見在武功縣南，西戎俯近，恐有異謀；

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard that in Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures he importunes military commissioners and prefectural and district officials as a beggar; he is now south of Wugong County, where the Western Rong press close— I fear he may harbor some irregular design.
translations.idiomatic: I have just learned that in Bin, Ning, Qing, and other prefectures he importunes commissioners and local officials like a mendicant; he is now south of Wugong County, where the Western Rong lie close at hand, and I fear he may be plotting some irregular design.

sentences.zh: 若不冒死奏聞，必恐覆臣家族。

translations.literal: Unless I risk death to memorialize the throne, I must surely fear the destruction of my entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Unless I risk my life to report this to the throne, I must surely fear the ruin of our whole clan.

sentences.zh: 」詔令京兆府錮身遞送黔州，付李模於僻遠州驅使，勿許東西。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Capital District office to imprison him bodily and escort him under guard to Qianzhou, to deliver him to Li Mo for labor in a remote prefecture, and not to permit him to travel east or west.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Capital District to imprison Fang Kui and escort him under guard to Qianzhou, to hand him over to Li Mo for forced service in a remote prefecture, and not to allow him to travel east or west.

sentences.zh: 雲逵元和元年拜右金吾衛大將軍，歲中改京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe Yunkui was appointed General of the Right Gold Crow Guard; within the year he was changed to Intendant of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe, Yunkui was appointed General of the Right Gold Crow Guard; within the year he was transferred to Intendant of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 五年五月卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year he died.

sentences.zh: 李益李益，肅宗朝宰相揆之族子。

translations.literal: Li Yi was a clansman of the chancellor Li Huaizai of Emperor Suzong's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was a kinsman of the Suzong-era chancellor Li Huaizai.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，長為歌詩。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and long excelled in lyric poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and for years excelled in lyric poetry.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，與宗人李賀齊名。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan he and his clansman Li He were equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhenyuan era he and his kinsman Li He were equally renowned.

sentences.zh: 每作一篇，為教坊樂人以賂求取。

translations.literal: Whenever he finished a piece, musicians of the Music Bureau would bribe to obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he finished a new poem, musicians of the Music Bureau would bribe their way to obtaining it.

sentences.zh: 唱為供奉歌詞。

translations.literal: They sang it as lyrics for court performance.
translations.idiomatic: They performed it as lyrics for the imperial entertainments.

sentences.zh: 其《征人歌》、《早行篇》，好事者畫為屏障；

translations.literal: His "Song of the Campaigner" and "On Setting Out Early" lovers painted as screen pictures.
translations.idiomatic: His "Song of the Campaigner" and "On Setting Out Early" were painted on screens by admirers.

sentences.zh: 「回樂峰前沙似雪，受降城外月如霜」之句，天下以為歌詞。

translations.literal: The lines "Before Huile Peak the sand is like snow; outside Shouxiang Fortress the moon is like frost" the realm took as song lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: The lines "Before Huile Peak the sand is like snow; outside Shouxiang Fortress the moon is like frost" were taken throughout the realm as song lyrics.

sentences.zh: 然少有癡病，而多猜忌，防閑妻妾，過為苛酷，而有散灰扃戶之譚聞於時，故時謂妒癡為「李益疾」；

translations.literal: Yet from youth he had an ailment of obsession, and was much given to suspicion; in guarding against his wives and concubines he went beyond severity into cruelty, and the tale of scattering ashes and bolting doors was heard in the age; therefore people of the time called jealous obsession "Li Yi's disease."
translations.idiomatic: Yet from youth he suffered an obsessive disorder and was much given to suspicion; in guarding his wives and concubines he went beyond severity into cruelty, and the story of scattering ashes and bolting doors was widely known—so contemporaries called jealous obsession "Li Yi's disease."

sentences.zh: 以是久之不調，而流輩皆居顯位。

translations.literal: Because of this he long went without regular appointment, while men of his generation all held conspicuous posts.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he long went without regular appointment, while men of his own generation all held conspicuous posts.

sentences.zh: 益不得意，北遊河朔，幽州劉濟辟為從事，常與濟詩而有「不上望京樓」之句。

translations.literal: Yi was discontented, traveled north to the Hebei region, and Liu Ji of Youzhou engaged him as staff officer; he often wrote poems with Ji and had a line reading "not ascending the Wangjing Tower."
translations.idiomatic: Discontented, Li Yi traveled north to the Hebei region; Liu Ji of Youzhou engaged him on his staff, and in poems to Ji he included the line "not ascending the Wangjing Tower."

sentences.zh: 憲宗雅聞其名，自河北召還，用為秘書少監、集賢殿學士。

translations.literal: Xianzong had long heard his name and summoned him back from Hebei, employing him as Vice Director of the Palace Library and Academic of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had long admired his reputation and summoned him back from Hebei, appointing him Vice Director of the Palace Library and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 自負才地，多所淩忽，為眾不容，諫官舉其幽州詩句，降居散秩。

translations.literal: He relied on his talent and standing and often looked down on others; the multitude could not bear him, and remonstrating officials cited his Youzhou verses, so he was demoted to a nominal post.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and standing, he often treated others with contempt; colleagues could not tolerate him, and remonstrating officials cited his Youzhou verses, so he was reduced to a nominal post.

sentences.zh: 俄復用為秘書監，遷太子賓客、集賢學士判院事，轉右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was again employed as Director of the Palace Library, was promoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and was transferred to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again made Director of the Palace Library, then promoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy, and finally transferred to Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太和初，以禮部尚書致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he retired as Minister of Rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he retired as Minister of Rites and died.

sentences.zh: 李賀李賀，字長吉，宗室鄭王之後。

translations.literal: Li He, styled Changji, was a descendant of the imperial house, after Prince Zheng of the Zong line.
translations.idiomatic: Li He, whose courtesy name was Changji, was a descendant of the imperial house in the line of Prince Zheng of the Zong clan.

sentences.zh: 父名晉肅，以是不應進士，韓愈為之作《諱辨》，賀竟不就試。

translations.literal: His father's name was Jinsu; on this account he was not to take the jinshi examination; Han Yu wrote the "Treatise on the Taboo" for him, yet He in the end did not attempt the examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father's name was Jinsu, which barred him from the jinshi examination; Han Yu wrote the "Treatise on the Taboo" on his behalf, yet Li He never sat for the examination.

sentences.zh: 手筆敏捷，尤長於歌篇。

translations.literal: His brush was swift, and he was especially skilled in lyric pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His brush was swift, and he was especially accomplished in lyric verse.

sentences.zh: 其文思體勢，如崇巖峭壁，萬仞崛起，當時文士從而效之，無能仿佛者。

translations.literal: The cast and momentum of his literary thought were like towering crags and sheer cliffs rising ten thousand ren; literary men of the time followed and imitated him, yet none could even approach him.
translations.idiomatic: The cast and force of his literary imagination were like sheer cliffs rising ten thousand feet; contemporaries tried to imitate him, yet none could even approach him.

sentences.zh: 其樂府詞數十篇，至於雲韶樂工，無不諷誦。

translations.literal: His yuefu lyrics numbered several tens of pieces; even the musicians of the Cloud Harmony Office all recited them from memory.
translations.idiomatic: His yuefu lyrics ran to several dozen pieces; even the musicians of the Cloud Harmony Office knew them by heart.

sentences.zh: 補太常寺協律郎，卒，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He was appointed Harmonizing Officer of the Grand Sacrifices Office and died at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Harmonizing Officer of the Grand Sacrifices Office and died at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 贊史臣曰：文學之士，代不乏才。

translations.literal: The chronicler's comment says: Men of letters have never lacked talent from age to age.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicler comments: Literary men have never been wanting from age to age.

sentences.zh: 永泰、貞元之間，如徐浩、趙涓諸公，可謂一時之秀也。

translations.literal: Between the Yongtai and Zhenyuan eras, such men as Xu Hao and Zhao Juan may be called the outstanding talents of a single generation.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yongtai and Zhenyuan eras, men such as Xu Hao and Zhao Juan may be called the outstanding talents of a single generation.

sentences.zh: 然太真以畏懦聞，邵說以僭侈失，于公異、呂渭、李益皆有微累，故知全其德者罕矣。

translations.literal: Yet Taizhen was known for timorousness, Shuo for loss through arrogant extravagance; Yu Gongyi, Lü Wei, and Li Yi all bore slight stains—thus one knows that those who preserve their virtue whole are rare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Taizhen was known for timidity, Shao Shuo for ruin through arrogant extravagance, and Yu Gongyi, Lü Wei, and Li Yi each carried minor blemishes—so one sees how rare it is to keep one's virtue intact.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：名以才顯，才兼德尊。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Name is displayed through talent; talent should be joined with honored virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: A name shines through talent, yet talent should be joined to honored virtue.

sentences.zh: 徐、趙、劉、李，厥聲遠聞。

translations.literal: Xu, Zhao, Liu, and Li—their fame was heard far off.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Zhao, Liu, and Li—their renown carried far.

sentences.zh: 邵、于、呂、鄭，其名久存。

translations.literal: Shuo, Yu, Lü, and Zheng—their names long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, Yu, Lü, and Zheng—their names long endure.

sentences.zh: 半乏全德，愧於後人。

translations.literal: Half lacking full virtue—they are ashamed before later men.
translations.idiomatic: Half lacking in full virtue—they stand ashamed before posterity.
